title: General Science & Ability
source: Part-I MCQs of the CSS General Science & Ability papers (cssforum.net). No official key was published, so the answers here were worked out by MPT-AI.

lessons.title: CSS GSA 2013 · Set 1
lessons.subtitle: CSS written-exam paper · answers worked out by MPT-AI

questions.prompt: Who proposed the concept “All motion is relative” ?
questions.explanation: Galilean relativity — Galileo argued that motion can only be described relative to another body. Einstein later generalised the idea.

questions.prompt: The field of specialization of famous Muslim scientist Abu Usman Aljahiz was:
questions.explanation: Abu Usman al-Jahiz wrote Kitab al-Hayawan (the Book of Animals), the founding work of Arabic zoology.

questions.prompt: Albatros is:
questions.explanation: The albatross is a large seabird with the longest wingspan of any living bird.

questions.prompt: The biggest planet in our solar system is:
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system — about 11 times the diameter of Earth.

questions.prompt: The biggest species of the cat family is:
questions.explanation: The tiger is the largest member of the cat family; the Siberian tiger is the biggest of all.

questions.prompt: Which group of animals has heterogametic females?
questions.explanation: Birds use the ZW system, so the female is ZW — heterogametic. In mammals the male (XY) is heterogametic.

questions.prompt: The dominant phase of life cycle in these organisms is haploid:
questions.explanation: In mosses the dominant, visible plant is the haploid gametophyte; the sporophyte stays attached and dependent.

questions.prompt: The atmosphere of moon consists of:
questions.explanation: The Moon has effectively no atmosphere — only a trace exosphere of helium, argon, neon and hydrogen. None of the listed mixtures is correct.

questions.prompt: The chemical name of quartz is:
questions.explanation: Quartz is crystalline silicon dioxide, SiO2.

questions.prompt: Which month of a calendar year can lack a new moon?
questions.explanation: A lunar month is about 29.5 days, so only February — at 28 or 29 days — can pass without a new moon.

lessons.title: CSS GSA 2013 · Set 2
lessons.subtitle: CSS written-exam paper · answers worked out by MPT-AI

questions.prompt: Deuterium differs from hydrogen in having:
choices: Different atomic number but same atomic weight
Different atomic number and different atomic weight
Same atomic number but different atomic weight
questions.explanation: Deuterium is an isotope of hydrogen: one proton (same atomic number) plus a neutron, so roughly double the mass.

questions.prompt: One of the following is a water soluble vitamin:
questions.explanation: A, D and K are all fat-soluble. The water-soluble vitamins are C and the B group, so none of the options fits.

questions.prompt: Coulomb is the scientific unit to measure:
questions.explanation: The coulomb measures electric charge, not velocity, temperature or mass.

questions.prompt: Equator passes through one of these countries:
questions.explanation: The equator crosses countries such as Ecuador, Kenya and Indonesia — not Saudi Arabia, Italy or Japan.

questions.prompt: Anti Diuretic hormone is secreted by one of the following glands:
questions.explanation: ADH (vasopressin) is made in the hypothalamus and released into the blood by the posterior pituitary.

questions.prompt: Basha Dam is to be constructed on:
questions.explanation: Diamer-Bhasha Dam is being built on the River Indus, not the Sutlej, Jhelum or Chenab.

questions.prompt: UV light falls in the category of:
questions.explanation: UV is conventionally classed as non-ionizing radiation, though the shortest UV-C wavelengths begin to ionize.

questions.prompt: The earth’s ---------------------- is divided into 15 major plates of various sizes:
questions.explanation: The lithosphere - the crust plus the rigid upper mantle - is broken into roughly 15 major tectonic plates.

lessons.title: CSS GSA 2024 · Set 1
lessons.subtitle: CSS written-exam paper · answers worked out by MPT-AI

questions.prompt: In fish liver oil there is:
questions.explanation: Fish liver oil is a rich source of both vitamin A and vitamin D.

questions.prompt: When day and night are equal?
questions.explanation: The equinoxes: about 21 March and 23 September, when the Sun is overhead at the equator.

questions.prompt: What are total number of combinations of 09 things taken 03 at a time?
questions.explanation: Combinations of 9 things taken 3 at a time = 9!/(3!x6!) = 84.

questions.prompt: The chemical formula for alum is:
questions.explanation: Potash alum is KAl(SO4)2.12H2O — a double sulphate of potassium and aluminium with twelve waters of crystallisation.

questions.prompt: If the radius of a circle is increased three times then its area is increased:
questions.explanation: Area scales with the square of the radius, so tripling the radius multiplies the area by 9.

questions.prompt: One degree of longitude on the equator is equal to a distance of:
questions.explanation: The equator is about 24,900 miles round and 360 degrees, so one degree is roughly 69 miles (111 km).

questions.prompt: The protein molecule is made of:
choices: Short range chain of amino acids
Long range chain of amino acids
questions.explanation: Proteins are long chains of amino acids joined by peptide bonds; short chains are peptides.

questions.prompt: The minimum amount of vitamin stored in the human body is of:
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is water-soluble and excreted rather than stored, so the body holds the smallest reserve of it.

questions.prompt: The pH of soil is raised using:
questions.explanation: Limestone (calcium carbonate) neutralises acidity, raising soil pH. Gypsum does not change pH appreciably.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is used for measuring distance?
questions.explanation: A light year is the distance light travels in a year. Coulomb measures charge, farad capacitance and curie radioactivity.

lessons.title: CSS GSA 2024 · Set 2
lessons.subtitle: CSS written-exam paper · answers worked out by MPT-AI

questions.prompt: Which of the following contains a greater number of carbon atoms in one mole of each compound?
questions.explanation: Ethanol (C2H5OH) has two carbon atoms per molecule; chloroform and methanol have one and water none.

questions.prompt: A pencil dipped in water appears bent due to:
questions.explanation: Light bends as it passes between water and air — refraction — so the submerged part appears displaced.

questions.prompt: Fishes die outside the water due to:
questions.explanation: Gills work only in water: out of it the filaments collapse and the fish cannot absorb dissolved oxygen.

questions.prompt: In dementia a person:
questions.explanation: Dementia is a progressive loss of thinking, memory and reasoning severe enough to disrupt daily life.

questions.prompt: Earthquake is measured by the instrument:
questions.explanation: A seismograph records the ground motion of an earthquake; the magnitude is then read off that record.

questions.prompt: A cyclone is formed:
choices: When the warm air rises upward over the ocean
When moist air rises upward over the ocean
When moist air pressed downward over the ocean
When warm, moist air rises upward over the ocean
questions.explanation: A cyclone forms where warm, moist air rises over the ocean, leaving low pressure that draws in more air.

questions.prompt: Why red light is used in traffic signal for danger?
choices: It has long wavelength and high frequency
It has long wavelength and short frequency
questions.explanation: Red has the longest wavelength of visible light, and therefore the lowest frequency; it scatters least, so it stays visible farthest.

questions.prompt: The heavy water is:
choices: Denoted by D₂O and contains simple hydrogen
Denoted by H₂O and contains deuterium
Denoted by D₂O and contains deuterium
Denoted by H₂O and contains simple hydrogen
questions.explanation: Heavy water is D2O — water in which both hydrogens are deuterium.

lessons.title: CSS GSA 2025 · Set 1
lessons.subtitle: CSS written-exam paper · answers worked out by MPT-AI

questions.prompt: Most major Tsunamis are produced by earthquakes with hypocenters less than:
questions.explanation: Most tsunami-generating earthquakes are shallow-focus, with hypocentres in the top 30 km of the crust.

questions.prompt: Which of the following source of energy is caused by uneven heating of earth’s surface?
questions.explanation: Uneven heating of the surface sets up pressure differences, and air moving between them is wind.

questions.prompt: Perinatal transmission is said to occur when a pathogen is transmitted from:
questions.explanation: Perinatal transmission passes an infection from mother to infant around the time of birth.

questions.prompt: Which of the plant group needs both land and water to complete their life cycle?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes (mosses and liverworts) live on land but need a film of water for their sperm to reach the egg.

questions.prompt: Maximum amount of carbohydrates are obtained from:
questions.explanation: Whole grains are largely starch, the richest of the listed sources of carbohydrate; nuts and plant oils are mostly fat.

questions.prompt: Which of the following class has the largest number of animals?
questions.explanation: Insects account for the majority of all described animal species — over a million of them.

questions.prompt: The process of preserving meat by stewing in a covered earthenware jug is called:
questions.explanation: Jugging is the old method of stewing meat slowly in a covered earthenware jug.

questions.prompt: All operating systems get their total memory initialized from:
questions.explanation: At power-on the BIOS runs POST, initialises the memory and hands a usable memory map to the operating system.

questions.prompt: The amount of data transmitted for a given amount of time is called:
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is the volume of data a channel can carry per unit of time.

questions.prompt: Which of the following products can be prepared using raw guava?
questions.explanation: Raw, under-ripe guava is high in pectin, so it sets well as both jam and jelly.

lessons.title: CSS GSA 2025 · Set 2
lessons.subtitle: CSS written-exam paper · answers worked out by MPT-AI

questions.prompt: Which of the following is used as a stabilizer in ice cream?
questions.explanation: Gelatin is a classic ice-cream stabiliser: it binds water and keeps ice crystals small.

questions.prompt: In the structure of fiber, the light is guided through the core due to total internal:
questions.explanation: An optical fibre guides light by total internal reflection at the core-cladding boundary.

questions.prompt: Who is known as the inventor of Artificial Intelligence?
questions.explanation: John McCarthy coined the term "artificial intelligence" in 1955 and is called its father.

questions.prompt: Cement factory labourer are prone to:
questions.explanation: Cement work exposes labourers to silica dust, causing silicosis (spelled "cytosilicosis" in the paper).

questions.prompt: The fastest enzyme is:
questions.explanation: Carbonic anhydrase is the fastest known enzyme, turning over up to a million molecules a second.

questions.prompt: Process of adding vitamins to milk is known as:
questions.explanation: Adding vitamins or minerals that were not originally present is fortification.

questions.prompt: The waves which are used for line of sight (LOS) communication are called:
questions.explanation: Space (direct) waves travel in a straight line from transmitter to receiver, which is what line-of-sight links use.
